claim: Family-level team effect correlates with the family's capability gap to the frontier (Study 1, exploratory D44/D45)

definition.capability_gap: mean composite F-S-N minus C-S-N per family (positive = cheap below frontier)
definition.team_effect: mean composite C-T-N minus F-S-N per family (team output vs frontier solo)
definition.team_lift: mean composite C-T-N minus C-S-N per family (structure effect within cheap tier)

source: results/exploratory_heterogeneity.json A1_reliability.cell_sd_cv (760-run exploratory subset, 19 problems, frozen 2026-08-22)
mechanical_note: team_effect = team_lift - gap by construction, so the gap-vs-team-effect correlation is partly mechanical; the non-mechanical content is that lifts only partially compensate the gap (r=+0.82).
discrepancies_fixed_in_v15: paper quoted claude gap as -0.357; under the gap definition that generates r=-0.978 it is +0.364 (claude cheap farthest BELOW frontier). -0.357 was the opposite-sign convention from full-data means.

paper prose said teams help most where cheap is 'farthest' from frontier (kimi) and hurt where gap is 'small' (claude); reversed. kimi gap -0.164 = cheap ABOVE frontier; claude gap +0.364 = farthest below.
